account: Clairity, Inc. of Austin, Texas, developed Allix5, deep learning software that reads a screening mammogram and predicts the chance that the patient will be diagnosed with breast cancer within five years. FDA reviewers describe a retrospective pivotal study of 77,511 exams from 44,112 patients at five screening sites in Atlanta, Fort Worth, Bedford, Sacramento and Folsom. None of these sites supplied data for training. Biopsy results and later mammograms served as the reference. The area under the time-dependent ROC curve was 0.70, above a performance goal of 0.64 based on the discrimination of traditional risk models. With current cancers excluded, the area was 0.66, and calibration met the pre-set tolerance in both groups. Black patients made up 37% of exams; the area was 0.67 for them and 0.73 for White patients. FDA granted the De Novo request on 30 May 2025. The study compared the software with a fixed goal drawn from traditional models, and the reviewers note that the software overestimated risk in the highest tenth of predictions for patients without current cancer.
